name: Aérospatiale SA341/342 Gazelle
summary: A fast, slender French light helicopter, best known for the first production fenestron tail and widely flown by civilian collectors and military operators.

wings: Three-blade rigid-looking main rotor with a low mast fairing
engines: Single turboshaft behind the cabin with a short exhaust on the roof
Intake and exhaust on the upper rear
fuselage: Slim, tapered fuselage with a big glazed nose and pointed profile
Five seats, skids on short struts
Large front doors and rear doors
tail: Fenestron (ducted fan) in the vertical fin with a small stabilizer

tellTales: Ducted tail fan on a narrow, tapered single-turbine helicopter
Slim fuselage with a pointed glazed nose
Three-blade rotor and skids, no wheels

confusedWith.howToTell: The EC120 has a rounder, bulbous egg-shaped nose and larger cabin; the Gazelle is slimmer and more angular.
The Dauphin is a big twin-engine helicopter with retractable wheels; the Gazelle is a small single-engine helicopter on skids.
The H125 has a conventional tail rotor and a tall boxy cabin; the Gazelle has a ducted fan and a slimmer, tapered body.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
